sections.h2: Where is Barrow County, Georgia, and what towns does it contain?
sections.html:
Barrow County sits in the east central part of Georgia, with Winder as its county seat, and it belongs to the Atlanta metropolitan statistical area. Voters approved the constitutional amendment creating it on November 3, 1914, and it was carved from parts of Gwinnett, Jackson and Walton counties. It was the 149th of the state's 159 counties, per Wikipedia.

The county is compact: 163 square miles in total, with 160 of them land, all within the Upper Oconee River sub-basin of the Altamaha River basin. Hall, Jackson, Oconee, Walton and Gwinnett counties border it, and Clarke County touches it at a single point.

  • Cities: Auburn, Statham and Winder
  • Towns: Bethlehem, Braselton (mostly in Jackson County) and Carl
  • Census-designated place: Russell
  • Unincorporated: Barrow Heights, Mulberry and Whistleville

Because Braselton reaches into three counties, a seller there should check the parcel record to see which county tax commissioner sends the bill.

sections.h2: How fast has Barrow County grown?
sections.html:
Barrow County has more than doubled in population since 2000. The decennial counts were 46,144 in 2000, 69,367 in 2010 and 83,505 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 99,773.

That growth sets Barrow County apart from rural Georgia counties such as Bacon County. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $294,700 for 2020 to 2024, 78.5 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, and the county issued 1,584 building permits in 2025. Population density is 518.5 people per square mile, against 39.2 in Bacon County.

A seller with a house in a newer subdivision near Winder or Auburn is selling into a market with many comparable homes, so condition and price carry more weight than in a rural county.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Barrow County homes?
sections.html:
Barrow County Schools is the only district covering the county. Its two high school clusters are named for Winder-Barrow High School and Apalachee High School, so a buyer's school assignment depends on which cluster the address falls in.

  • Winder-Barrow cluster: Winder-Barrow High, Richard B. Russell Middle, Bear Creek Middle, and Holsenbeck, Bramlett, Statham, County Line and Winder elementary schools
  • Apalachee cluster: Apalachee High, Westside Middle, Haymon-Morris Middle, and Auburn, Kennedy, Bethlehem and Yargo elementary schools
  • Barrow Arts and Sciences Academy

The district list comes from Wikipedia, so confirm school zones with the district before you advertise one in a listing.

sections.h2: Who bills and who assesses property in Barrow County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's main office is at 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. The Barrow County Tax Portal lists (770) 307-3106 and hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday. Card payments add a 2.5 percent service fee with a $1.50 minimum.

The Tax Assessors Office uses the same 30 N. Broad Street address, and the county says it takes calls from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Parcel values and assessment notices can be viewed and printed from qPublic. The county's online tax pages also say that vehicle transactions require a valid Georgia driver's license or ID card showing a Barrow County address, which matters if you are a new resident updating a tag after buying.

The tax commissioner sets the due date and mails the bill. It does not set your value; that belongs to the assessors.

sections.h2: When do Barrow County assessment notices and tax bills go out?
sections.html:
The county's 2024 announcement said assessment notices for real property, along with notices for personal property such as aircraft, boats and business equipment, were mailed on May 1, and that final tax bills would not go out until September and would not be due until November. Treat that as the usual rhythm and check your own bill for the exact date.

An assessment notice is not a tax bill. It gives an estimate of taxes based on the assessed value. Owners who disagree have a 45-day window to appeal, and appeals can be filed online through qPublic, by mail, or in person at the Tax Assessors Office.

  • Appeal grounds under Georgia law: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption
  • Routes: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator
  • The Department of Revenue cannot override the board, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or the court on an individual value

sections.h2: What should Barrow County sellers know about city and county bills?
sections.html:
Property inside a city may be taxed by the city as well as the county, so ask the city clerk whether the city issues its own bill. Barrow County has three cities and three towns. Never assume a payoff from the county includes any municipal balance.

Georgia's Department of Revenue says an owner on January 1 owes tax for the entire year, even if the house sells on January 2, and it does not allow a refund for a part-year owner. The practical step is to have the title company ask for a current payoff from each billing office and pay both at closing.

If an older bill is unpaid, the county tax commissioner's office can tell you whether a lien has been recorded.

sections.h2: What happens to extra money from a Barrow County tax sale?
sections.html:
The county's real property page says it works with Weissman Excess Funds Management on excess funds that result from tax sales. Records of those funds can be viewed on the firm's site, and the county says the list is typically updated on the 1st and 15th of each month.

To request information, the page says to send an email. It also states plainly that Barrow County does not release excess funds to third parties. Anyone who lost a house to a tax sale should contact the Tax Commissioner's Office or the firm directly about a claim; do not pay a stranger to claim it for you.

sections.h2: How do exemptions work in Barrow County?
sections.html:
Georgia offers a standard homestead exemption to people who own and occupy their home as a primary residence, and many counties add larger local ones. File with the tax commissioner or the assessors, whichever your county designates, and ask which applies in Barrow County.

The state formula subtracts the homestead amount from the assessed value, then applies the millage rate. Georgia's Department of Revenue explains that exemptions are filed with the county tax commissioner or the county tax assessor's office. Call (770) 307-3106 to confirm which office takes applications, and bring proof of residency.

faqs.q: Where is the Barrow County tax office?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner is at 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. The phone is (770) 307-3106 and the office is open from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: Is an assessment notice a tax bill in Barrow County?
faqs.a: No. The county says the notice is an estimate of taxes based on assessed value. Final bills are mailed later in the year, in September according to the county's 2024 announcement.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Barrow County value?
faqs.a: File within 45 days of the notice. You can appeal online through qPublic, by mail, or in person at the Tax Assessors Office at 30 N. Broad Street, Winder.

faqs.q: Does Barrow County release excess tax sale funds to third parties?
faqs.a: No. The county's own page says it does not release excess funds to third parties, and routes claims through the Tax Commissioner's Office and its excess funds partner.

faqs.q: Who owes tax if I sell my Barrow County house in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 owes the full year under Georgia law, and no refund is given for a partial year. Split the bill with the buyer in your closing paperwork.
